$comment: AoE2 DE mod-toolkit intent schema. EXTERNALIZED ON PURPOSE: game patches change format details, and a version bump must be a data edit, not a code change. The compiler reads this file; nothing about an intent is hard-coded in Python.

unit.stat.title: 改变单位属性
unit.stat.description: Adjust one numeric stat on every civilization's copy of a unit.

unit.label: 单位
unit.help: Name or id. Ambiguity is reported, never guessed.

stat.label: 属性
stat.help: Range and reload are float32 (fractions are allowed). reload_time is SECONDS BETWEEN ATTACKS, so a smaller number is a faster unit -- an intent UI should offer 'attack faster' rather than a raw negative. min_range is a dead zone: 0 means the unit can fire at any distance. accuracy is a whole percent (100 = always hits). garrison_capacity is how many units a building or ram can shelter; it is a single byte, so it caps at 255 and 0 means 'cannot shelter anyone' (most records).

value.label: 设为
value.help: Absolute new value. Mutually exclusive with 'delta'.

civs.label: 文明
civs.help: Default 'all'. Editing one civ only is almost never what a user means.

compile.note: Each civilization holds an INDEPENDENT physical record, so one logical edit fans out to N civs.

unit.attack_class.title: 改变单位的攻击/护甲数值
unit.attack_class.title_en: Change a unit's attack or armour value
unit.attack_class.description: Adjust the raw attack/armour entry for a specific armour class.

class_id.label: 类别
class_id.help: Read from schema/armor_classes.json. Unknown ids render as 'Class N'.

resource.$comment: No 'population' here, unlike unit.cost which has five. That is measured, not an oversight: no technology in the shipped data charges population. _probe/test_declared_resources.py walks every cost slot of every tech and unit record and fails unless this option set is EXACTLY what tech records actually charge -- so a game update that starts charging population on a tech becomes a test failure, instead of an intent that silently cannot reach the new slot.

command.help: Which entry of this tech's effect list to change. A tech's effect record is a list of commands, and the same (attribute, target, operation) triple can appear on it twice with different numbers ('C-Bonus, Military cost -20%' multiplies food cost by 1.174 and again by 0.800). Any scheme that addressed a command by its meaning would therefore have to guess in 12 of the shipped techs, so the address is the position in the list the user picked from. Read the list with Toolkit.effects(tech).

unit.availability.title: 改变某个文明能否建造某单位
unit.availability.title_en: Change whether a civilization can build a unit
unit.availability.description: Give or take away a unit for ONE civilization. Both directions write THREE layers at once: the .dat recipe the user confirmed in game, the CivTechTrees file, and the build panel. A grant appends an enable and moves the unit's training button; a revoke appends a disable hung on a technology that fires later than the one making the unit available.

unit.label: 单位
unit.help: Name or id. Only units that appear in at least one civilization's tech tree can be granted: 1364 of the 1651 name-resolved units do not, and the refusal says exactly that instead of calling them unknown.

civ.label: 文明
civ.help: Exactly one civilization name, as the .dat spells it (British, Hindustanis, Magyars) or its CivTechTrees file name. Unlike the stat intents this is never 'all'.

action.label: 操作
action.help: grant = make it buildable, revoke = make it not buildable. Granting copies a real row from a civilization that has it; no field value is ever invented.

compile.why_not_dat: The unit RECORD carries no per-civ availability byte: across 2693 unit ids only 7 differ between civilizations in the Enabled/Disabled bytes, while British and Goths differ on 24 ids. The .dat expresses it elsewhere -- a civ-owned free technology carrying a `type 2` enable command -- which is the recipe below. Measured in _probe/probe_availability_decisive.py and _probe/test_civ_unit_gate.py.

dat_half.write_operations_note: Each action declares its own count above, because the two recipes write different numbers. GRANT writes two: one new Effect record, then the re-pointed technology -- the training ButtonID byte is part of that same recipe rather than a third operation. REVOKE writes ONE: one new Effect record carrying the carrier's commands plus `type 2 b=0`, then the re-pointed technology; there is no button to move, because the unit has to disappear rather than shift. Both numbers are declared rather than measured, because measuring them serialises the whole 93 MB .dat (25 s) while a preview must stay cheap; `_probe/test_dat_half_count.py` asserts each declaration still equals `len(apply_grant(...)["edits"])` and `len(apply_revoke(...)["edits"])`, so the two cannot drift apart silently.
dat_half.help: GRANT: append a NEW effect carrying the anchor technology's own commands plus 'type 2, unit, 1' and re-point that technology at it, then move the unit's training button to a free slot (a byte patch, because the writer's model does not carry train_locations). REVOKE: append a NEW effect carrying the carrier technology's own commands plus 'type 2, unit, 0' and re-point that technology at it -- no button byte, because the unit has to disappear rather than move. The carrier for a revoke MUST fire LATER than whatever makes the unit available, or the enable overwrites the disable; `datgrant.pick_revoke_tech` enforces that ordering and refuses, with a reason, when no such carrier exists. EnablingResearch is deliberately left alone in both directions: the confirmed grant recipe wrote no such byte, and the field is global per unit id, so pointing it at one civilization's technology would claim that all 63 are enabled by it.
dat_half.why_enabling_research_is_not_written: Three measurements, in _probe/probe_enabling_scope.py. (1) `dsh test v7`, the recipe the user confirmed in game (m27131), wrote no EnablingResearch byte at all -- its script patches only when the shipped value is not -1, and unit 2550 ships as -1. (2) The field does not gate: v5 set it to the age-gated tech 263 and v6 cleared it to -1, and both behaved identically in game. (3) It is one connection per unit id, not per civilization, so writing British's private tech 383 onto unit 2550 -- which Incas/Mapuche/Muisca/Tupi build and the British do not -- would create a pairing the shipped corpus contains zero of.
dat_half.why_not_for_other_actions: The technology space has no `.dat` half in either direction: both proven commands are unit-space (`type 2` names a UNIT id), so pointing one at a tech node would enable or disable whichever unit happens to share that integer. That is why tech.availability declares no dat_half at all while this intent declares one.
dat_half.verified_in_game: GRANT: 2026-10-16, `dsh test v7` -- villagers stayed at 1000 hp, the Castle Longbowman was unaffected, and the Dark Age Barracks showed the Champi Scout. REVOKE: 2026-10-19, `dsh test v17` -- the Incas still had the Champi Scout in the Dark Age and had LOST it in the Castle Age, because the same disable was hung on two carriers that fire at different times. Both carriers were byte-verified present in the shipped .dat, so firing time is the only thing that differed between the two readings -- the ordering rule is part of the result, not an assumption.

tech.availability.title: 改变某个文明能否研究某科技
tech.availability.title_en: Change whether a civilization can research a technology
tech.availability.description: Give or take away a technology for ONE civilization. Like unit.availability this changes no .dat BYTE, but it addresses the OTHER id space: a tech row's Node ID is the .dat tech ARRAY INDEX, and the same integer is a unit id in the unit space, so the two must never be mixed.

tech.label: 科技
tech.help: Name or id. 238 distinct tech nodes are listed across the 62 CivTechTrees files; a tech that is in no civilization's tree cannot be granted and the refusal says exactly that.

civ.label: 文明
civ.help: Exactly one civilization name, as the .dat spells it (British, Hindustanis, Magyars) or its CivTechTrees file name. Never 'all'.

action.label: 操作
action.help: grant = make it researchable, revoke = remove it from the tree. Granting copies a real row from a civilization that has it; no field value is ever invented.

compile.why_not_dat: Same reason as unit.availability: the .dat holds one GLOBAL tech record and no per-civ byte, so 62 identical records cannot express 'civ X may research this'. Measured in _probe/probe_tech_rows.py (5244 tech rows, 238 distinct ids, none outside the .dat array).
compile.why_no_dat_half: Unlike unit.availability's grant, no recipe here has ever been confirmed in game, so this intent declares no dat_half at all and edits no .dat byte. It is not the same claim as 'no .dat is present': a tech row lives under the DAT storage point, and a mod that overrides that folder without empires2_x2_p1.dat makes the game fail to start (mod/emitter.py), so the emitter always carries the base .dat along -- byte-identical, hence dat_is_carrier and never changes_dat. `_probe/test_availability_dat_half.py` checks this against the bytes, because `mod_contains_dat` here said `false` while the disk said otherwise.

unit.sprite.title: 换掉单位的造型
unit.sprite.title_en: Make one unit look like another
unit.sprite.description: Copy another unit's animation files over this one's, so it is drawn as that unit while keeping its own stats. Writes loose .sld files under resources/_common/drs/graphics and no .dat at all.

unit.label: 单位
unit.help: The unit whose look changes. Name or id; ambiguity is reported, never guessed.

donor.label: 变成
donor.help: The unit to copy the look FROM. Its animation files are copied onto the target's, matched one animation at a time by the engine's own animation name (walkA onto walkA). A donor that lacks an animation the target has leaves the target's own picture there, and the report says which.

civs.label: 文明
civs.help: Optional. Omit for every civilization. This matters because the same unit id is not always the same art: unit 4 is u_arc_archer for 57 civilizations and u_arc_bowman for the six Chronicles ones, so asking for all of them can legitimately be a contradiction (one file cannot hold two pictures) and is refused with both pictures named rather than silently picking one.

whole_family.label: 连干活的样子也换
whole_family.help: Optional, default off. A unit that swaps records when it is given a job (a villager is 27 records carrying 18 different pictures: Villager Male, Builder Male, Lumberjack Male, GoldMiner Male, Farmer Male ...) is only fully re-skinned when every one of those records is rewritten. Off, this sentence replaces the unit's ordinary picture and the report names exactly which jobs keep the old look. On, every record in the unit's family is rewritten -- for the villager that measured 466 files and 418 MB instead of 20 files and 18 MB. Both numbers are real: measured on the shipped install, not estimated. Asking for the family also turns on `fill`, because without it the family scope still cannot deliver: see that field.

fill.label: 缺的动画拿相近的补
fill.help: Optional. When the donor has no picture for an animation the target needs, let a nearby animation of the SAME donor stand in for it (carry <- walk, work <- attack, idlec <- idle). Defaults to on when `whole_family` is on, off otherwise. This is not a nicety: a villager family needs ten animations and NO entity in the game owns all ten -- `seed` exists on 4 unit ids, `task` on 6, `carry` on 36, `work` on 61 -- so a family reskin without filling leaves five animations on the shipped human art, and the villager turns back into a person the moment it works. Measured in game on 2026-10-17. A stand-in is rejected unless its angle count matches and it has at least as many frames, because the engine indexes the sprite by the RECORD's frame and angle counts: too few frames is unrenderable garbage, while extra frames are simply never asked for.

mode.label: 交付方式
mode.help: HOW the new picture reaches the game, and the two answers are different products. `copy` ships the donor's art once per target filename: proven in game on 2026-10-17, ships no .dat, and therefore coexists with every other data mod -- the villager family is 466 files and 418 MB. `rename` rewrites the graphics records' `file` strings to point at pictures the game already has: 244 record edits, the .dat gets 2,514 bytes SMALLER, the whole mod is 11 MB -- but it ships a .dat, and the game loads one data mod per match, so it cannot sit alongside a resource-multiplier or civ-overhaul mod. Default is `copy` because it is the proven and the non-conflicting one; the cheap model must be asked for. Both produce the same picture on screen (verified in game).

compile.why_not_dat: A unit's picture is not in the .dat at all: the 93 MB file only carries the NAME of the art (the standing graphic's `file` string, via a graphics record's id). The picture itself is a loose uncompressed .sld under resources/_common/drs/graphics, so the whole edit is 'copy these files over those files'. Nothing in the .dat has to change, which also means this mod cannot break on a game update that only rebalances numbers.
compile.per_civ_reason: 370 of 2693 unit ids have a different standing graphic in different civilizations, so the set of target filenames is computed per civilization and unioned.
compile.resource_variants: Also copied: the art an entity uses ONLY while carrying a resource (StoneMiner Male has one file of its own, and no unit record names it). Found and shipped in `dsh test v12`; 4 stems in the game carry one, 8 files for the villager family.
compile.in_bundle_note: This sentence can sit inside a plan_bundle/build_bundle list next to .dat and CivTechTrees sentences, and all of them land in one mod folder with no second emitter. Two reskin sentences naming the SAME target file with different donors are refused by Toolkit._sprite_bundle with BOTH sentences quoted -- reskin.plan only checks within one sentence and cannot see across sentences, so without that second guard the later sentence would overwrite the earlier one in silence.
compile.bundle_edit_count_note: edit_count for a reskin is FILES, not bytes. A bundle must sum it with the byte patcher's edits and the availability .dat halves, or the preview and the build disagree.
compile.verified_in_game: 2026-10-17, `dsh test v10` (villager -> sheep, 20 loose .sld, no .dat): the game drew the sheep. The villager was a sheep while standing and while attacking and a human while chopping, mining and building -- which proved the loose override AND exposed that one record's art is not one unit's art.
compile.verified_detail: The override itself is PROVEN. What the first version got wrong is scope: unit 83's family spans 27 records and 18 stems, and replacing only the Villager Male stem left every task-specific record on its shipped human art. The engine never refuses; it simply draws whatever the record it re-pointed to names.

unit.art.title: 给单位画一张新图
unit.art.title_en: Paint a picture onto a unit's animations
unit.art.description: Take one picture off the user's disk and paint it onto the .sld files this unit is drawn from. The original motion survives: every frame keeps its own rect, so the picture is sampled in CANVAS coordinates and each frame's existing crop decides which part of it that frame shows. Writes loose .sld files and no .dat.

unit.label: 单位
unit.help: The unit to paint. Its animations are found the same way a reskin finds them: the unit record's standing graphic, through the graphics record's `file` string. A unit whose art is not a loose .sld (legacy names such as ARROW_NN) is refused with that reason rather than painted.

picture.label: 图片
picture.help: A PNG, JPEG or BMP on disk. It is scaled to FIT the box the original art occupies on the canvas, aspect ratio kept and centred, so a picture of any size lands where the original stood. The box is measured from the union of every frame's rect -- not guessed, and not the file's canvas, because a 200x200 canvas holds the art only in roughly x 68..132, y 52..108.

civs.label: 文明
civs.help: Optional. Omit for every civilization. This matters for pictures exactly as it does for reskins: 302 of 2,273 unit ids are drawn from a different file depending on the civilization, so the set of files to paint is computed per civilization and unioned. A file two civilizations share is painted once.

animations.label: 只改这些动作
animations.help: Optional. Limits the repaint to named animations (idle, walk, attack, death, decay, work, carry ...). The key is the ENGINE's own animation name from the graphics record -- 'Archer (Walk)' -> walk -- and not the filename suffix, because the shipped files spell the same animation both ways (u_arc_archer_walkA vs u_arc_bowman_walk). Omit to paint every animation the unit has.

compile.why_not_dat: An .sld cannot be built from scratch: every frame carrying a `main` layer also carries an `unknown2` layer (4,737,215 frames, zero exceptions in the shipped corpus) and unknown2's size is not a function of main's run list, so it cannot be regenerated. What CAN be done is to repaint the BC1 blocks of `main` in place and keep every other byte: shadow, playercolor, damage, unknown2, frame headers, padding and the frame grid all survive untouched.
compile.why_not_copy: Copying another unit's art is `unit.sprite`. This is the other half of that layer: a picture the game has never seen. It needs an encoder, and only the main layer has a proven one.
compile.bundle_edit_count_note: edit_count is FILES (each .sld counts once), like `unit.sprite` in copy mode.
compile.encoder_note: The block order is not free: a frame's run list places blocks on a grid of ceil(rect/4) cells in row-major order, and the payload is padded to ceil4. Both rules were proven by copying the original blocks back and reproducing the file byte-for-byte, which fails if either is off by one.
compile.grid_rule: A repaint must match the frame's own grid: the block count is fixed by the run list, so a picture of another size cannot be poured in without deciding what the extra pixels mean. Frames whose grid differs are skipped and reported, never stretched.
compile.x2_note: x1 and x2 are independent DRAWINGS, not scales of each other: over 6 shipped pairs the frame rects were exactly 2x in only 0-37 frames of 481-961. The engine derives the _x2 name from _x1, so both are painted, each at its own canvas size, from the same picture.
compile.not_verified_reason: A repainted .sld has not been loaded by a running game. Loose .sld loading itself IS proven (2026-10-17, `dsh test v10`/`v12`), but those mods copied shipped files; nothing in this project has yet put a hand-encoded block into a file the game then drew.

unit.create.title: 照着现成的单位做一个新单位
unit.create.title_en: Create a unit that the game does not have
unit.create.description: Clone one of a civilization's unit records into an id nothing uses, then name it.  The clone keeps the donor's class, animations, sounds and armour classes.  Its train location starts as the donor's, and the `builder`/`button` fields move it to another building or box.

donor.label: 照着做
donor.help: The unit to copy the record from. A clone is a BYTE IMAGE of this record with the id and the name id patched, so a unit whose record has a type-dependent tail (type 50, projectile, building) clones correctly without this tool deciding what each field means.

civ.label: 文明
civ.help: Exactly one civilization. A unit table is per-civilization, so a clone belongs to one civ's table -- adding it to all 63 is 63 records and 63 flag flips, a bigger edit this intent does not pretend to do. Loop over civs to do that.

name.label: 名字
name.help: The name the game will show. It ships as a loose key-value-modded-strings file for every locale the install has, plus English as the documented global fallback, which is the game's own supported way for a mod to add a string.

hp.label: 生命值
hp.help: Optional. The clone's hit points, patched into the record image at its fixed offset. Omit to keep the donor's.

button.label: 第几格
button.help: Optional. Which numbered box of the builder's command card the new unit should occupy. Omit to leave it on the donor's own number. The build moves EVERY train location the clone copied, because moving only the first would leave the rest on the donor's buttons -- the thing this field exists to change. A donor whose training slot points at no building (builder -1) is refused rather than silently left unreachable; 683 of the 2,164 British records are like that, so it is the common case and not an edge.

builder.label: 放在哪座建筑
builder.help: Optional. Which building shows the button, when that is not the one the donor uses. A unit's train location -- the entry that names the building, the box number and the train time -- lives on the UNIT's own record, so re-pointing it rewrites two bytes of the clone the build already writes; it does not touch the building and it appends nothing. So a building that never trained the donor can still show the clone. Omit to keep the donor's building.

compile.why_not_dat: This one DOES write the .dat: a unit record is a variable-length structure inside a per-civ record run, so it cannot be expressed as an in-place patch. It appends one record and flips one 4-byte slot.
compile.why_append_is_safe: A civ's unit table is a FIXED-SIZE array of per-id existence flags (measured: 2,750 slots for ids 0..2749, every non-zero value is 1) followed by the records in slot order. Appending a record therefore changes no offset in that array -- it only needs the flag flipped. Measured 2026-10-21: donor 83 into civ 1 is +2,387 bytes, the stream is consumed exactly, the result re-parses, the new id reads back with the donor's class, and re-serialising is byte-stable (delta +0).
compile.record_boundaries: Record lengths come from `locate.walk_unit`'s own extent, which was verified against the shipped file: for both civ 0 (2,693 records) and civ 1 (2,164), every record's end equals the next record's start. Rebuilding a record from field values is deliberately NOT done, because its tail is type-dependent and each field would be a guess.
compile.id_choice: The id must be one NO civilization uses and nothing points at. A hole in one civ is not a hole: British alone has 586, and the lowest is 43 -- but 43 is a real unit in Gaia and most other civs, so a clone there would make one id mean two different things. Of the 57 ids no record uses, 17 are named by shipped effect commands, a tech-tree node or the build panel, leaving 40 truly free; the lowest with a unit-header slot is 382. `_probe/test_new_unit.py` pins the whole selection.
compile.why_ships_strings: The record names itself by a STRING ID, so a clone without a string shows as the donor's name or as nothing. The game's own modded-string file is the supported add-a-string route (its shipped 605-byte instructions say so), and zh/en/tw each end at id 30030001, so 30030002 is the first id no locale uses.
compile.what_it_cannot_do: The icon has two halves and only the bytes are proven.  When the `icon` field names a picture, the build ships three files the game does not have -- the picture as an uncompressed BGRA DDS, plus the WHOLE merged icons.json and materials.json, because the engine reads a mod's complete tables and not a patch -- and the clone's record is written to the new slot with a read-back check.  Measured: the DDS decodes back pixel for pixel, the slot and its material resolve inside the built mod, every shipped slot and material is unchanged, and the record reads back 1000.  NOT measured: a running game drawing that icon, because no run has yet loaded a unit whose icon came from this path.  Without the `icon` field the clone draws the donor's icon.  Its place in a build menu follows the donor unless the `builder` field names another building: the train location is on the clone's own record, so re-pointing it rewrites two bytes there and never touches the building.
compile.bundle_edit_count_note: edit_count is RECORDS plus FLAGS: one appended record and one flag slot, so 2 -- not the byte count, which a caller cannot compare against other intents.
compile.not_verified_reason: A unit built by THIS method -- the bundle path -- has not been installed and loaded: `_probe/tmp_product_check.py` built v35 and never installed it.  What IS measured: the same `newunit` append+clone code produced `dsh test v26`..`v33`, which the user loaded and read in game (the unit appeared on the town centre's fourth button and could be trained), and the stream re-parses here with the unmodified parser, the clone reads back with the donor's fields and the re-pointed building, and the resulting file re-serialises byte-stably.  The icon path adds a second unmeasured half: its three shipped files are checked byte for byte and the record reads back the new slot, but no run has watched the game draw that icon.

tech.toggle_group.title: 把几项科技做成只能研究其中一个
tech.toggle_group.title_en: Make several technologies an exclusive group
tech.toggle_group.description: Makes the engine allow only one of several technologies. Measured 2026-10-22 on a real match: researching one then removes the others from the technology panel (they disappear), and they cannot be researched. The blocking half is a `type 102` disable command written on every member's own effect -- the same shape the 16 shipped MutuallyExclusive/Toggleable groups use. The linkedTechs.json record is written too, because that is what makes the UI show the red cross on a sibling; on its own it does NOT block anything (measured: JSON alone showed the cross and still let both be researched).

techs.label: 科技
techs.help: Two or more technologies. Fewer than two is not a choice, so it is refused rather than written as a group nobody can pick from.

type.label: 分组方式
type.help: MutuallyExclusive = researching one closes the others (the shipped Paphos groups). Toggleable = they switch each other on and off. Both are blocked with `type 102` commands. Cycle = they rotate in order; shipped Cycle groups carry no `type 102` at all, so a Cycle group is written as the linkedTechs record only and nothing here claims it blocks a research.

comment.label: 备注
comment.help: Written into the file's Comment field. It is documentation, not a mechanic: the engine ignores it (Pompeii reuses one NameId for a different group), so nothing depends on it.

compile.why_not_dat: type 102 does express 'disable a technology', and the shipped Toggleable groups use it (tech 1202 effect 1192 carries one command per sibling). Writing it that way needs an effect id, a required-tech list and a button slot per technology -- three couplings that can each be wrong separately. This layer states the same thing in one record.
compile.what_it_does_not_prove: That a group ADDED by a mod is honoured on the very first turn after install (v47 researched after a fresh launch, 2026-10-23), and that a CYCLE group does anything: v47 measured MutuallyExclusive (the sibling disappears) but no run has been made with Type=Cycle, and the shipped Cycle groups carry no `type 102` at all.

notes.label: 为什么没有「变灰」这个选项
notes.text: A greyed-out button in this game means 'a prerequisite is missing', and a prerequisite is a POSITIVE gate: `74 requires 67` orders two technologies, it cannot forbid one of them. Measured on the shipped data: 1147 of 1510 technologies have at least one prerequisite, and there is no pair anywhere that requires each other (the only apparent one is tech 0 referencing itself), so the engine never expresses 'either A or B' through prerequisites. Only `type 102` can forbid, and forbidding removes the button rather than greying it.

tech.create.title: 做一项游戏里没有的科技
tech.create.title_en: Create a technology that the game does not have
tech.create.description: Append one technology record modelled on an existing one, give it its own name string, its own effect and a research location so a building can research it. The record is addressed by its POSITION in the array, so the new id is the shipped count.

donor.label: 照着做
donor.help: The technology to copy the record shape from. Costs, required techs and the internal scaffolding are taken from it; the name, the effect and the research location are yours.

name.label: 名字
name.help: The name the game shows. It ships as a loose key-value-modded-strings file for every locale the install has, plus English as the documented global fallback.

building.label: 在哪座建筑里研究
building.help: Optional. Omit it and the new technology keeps the donor's research location, which is the only evidence the sentence gave about where it should appear.

research_time.label: 研究时间
research_time.help: Seconds. Omit it and the donor's time is kept.

button.label: 第几格
button.help: Which box on that building's card. Omit it and the donor's box is used, which is why the new technology shows up where the donor already was.

effect.label: 效果
effect.help: Optional shorthand for the effect's single command, as '<type>,<a>,<b>,<c>,<d>' -- for example '4,0,3,-1,1' is '+1 building armour'. Omit it and the new technology has no effect of its own, which is a legal state the shipped data also uses (330 technologies point at no effect).

compile.why_not_dat: The record HAS to be in the .dat: a technology is an array position, so there is no file in the dat directory that can add one. What the other layers can do is name it (the modded string table) and place it on a card (the record's own research_locations), and both are shipped with it.
compile.what_it_does_not_prove: That a created technology survives a GAME UPDATE. A technology is an array position, so its id is only the first free one against TODAY's shipped count -- a patch that adds technologies can move it. Whether the engine shows it on a card is no longer in doubt: dsh test v49 (2026-10-22) put it on the town centre's 8th research box and the user read it there.

notes: A technology is addressed by its array position, so the new id is the shipped count (1,510 today) and it moves whenever a patch adds technologies. The node id for a tree row is free: measured 2026-10-23, no CivTechTrees row in any of the 62 civilizations carries 1510 in the Unit space or the Tech space, and no shipped tech row is above 1509. The .dat record at index 1510 is the unit 'CityGate NE (Rubble)', which is a different space -- `civtechtrees.py`'s UNIT_USE_TYPES/TECH_USE_TYPES note is what keeps those two apart. This intent writes the .dat side only because the tree half has not been written yet, not because it collides.
The tech-tree research counter is a u8 with 14 rows of headroom. This intent does not add a tree row, so it does not spend any of it.

mod.note: Mod folder contents mirror the GAME ROOT directly; do not add an extra 'resources' wrapper beyond the mirrored path.

rules.separate_mods_reason: REFUTED 2026-10-23. This used to claim the game's mod manager warns (IDS_MODMGR_DATAMOD_SCENARIO_WARNING / _UNEXPECTED_WARNING) that mixing data mods with scenario/UI mods misbehaves. The string says 「警告。您将加载一个带有非官方数据集的场景。」 -- it is about a scenario carrying its own data set, not about one mod folder holding two kinds of file. Measured: two shipped third-party mods (310130_1233 For Stephen Chow, 445153_4X科技...) each put a .dat and text tables in one folder, and this project's dsh test v49 (.dat + 17 locale string tables in one folder) was verified in game. One folder may carry several layers; the emitter now reports them in manifest['layers'].

verification.note: Compression is NOT byte-reproducible, so never validate by recompressing and comparing. Always reparse.
